run.question:
EU prod is having a checkout incident — 500s on POST /api/checkout. Investigate
using the app-267-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The requested index app-267-prod-logs is the only index on the Elasticsearch source and contains exactly 4 documents in the authorized window; all four self-identify as cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1, matching EU prod. Read together they describe one chain: at 2026-11-23T15:54:17Z payment-service logged "Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms" and checkout-service logged "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)"; at 16:54:17Z checkout-service logged "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)"; at 17:24:17Z payment-service logged a WARN that adyen-eu degraded mode was acknowledged via the provider status page with retry queue depth=620. Supported hypothesis: the checkout 500s are a consequence of payment-service's upstream calls to the external provider adyen-eu timing out at 30s, not of a local pod fault. Counter-evidence against local causes: in the readable cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1 the checkout and payment deployments are 1/1 ready, both pods Running with 0 restarts and no previous container instance, payment's own stdout logs show repeated successful charges with no error lines, and no fault-injection flag for payment is switched on (flagd paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable both defaultVariant off). Caveats that keep this partial: Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for the whole run, so no error-rate, latency or span evidence could confirm or time the failure; the log documents name services "checkout-service"/"payment-service" and provider adyen-eu, none of which exist as objects in the readable cluster, so the emitting workloads could not be inspected directly; and only 4 log lines exist, so the start of the adyen-eu degradation and its full impact are unknown.

claims.text: app-267-prod-logs is the only index on the Elasticsearch source (4 documents, green) and the whole-window match_all search returned exactly 4 documents, every one tagged cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, environment=prod, region=eu-west-1; timestamps run 2026-11-23T15:54:17Z to 2026-11-23T17:24:17Z.
checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T15:54:17Z: "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)".
payment-service logged ERROR at the same instant 2026-11-23T15:54:17Z: "Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms".
checkout-service logged ERROR at 2026-11-23T16:54:17Z: "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)".
payment-service logged WARN at 2026-11-23T17:24:17Z: "adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620".

In cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1, deployments checkout and payment (namespace otel-demo) each show 1 ready of 1 replica, and their pods checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm are phase Running, container ready=true, restartCount=0, with no last terminated state ("no previous instance" reported for both).

The newest 40 lines of pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (covering 2026-11-23T17:39:14Z to 17:53:51Z) are alternating info-level "Charge request received." and "Transaction complete." entries with no error, timeout, adyen or circuit-breaker text.

The only checkout-pod line matched by the error/fail/timeout/adyen/circuit/500 regex in 15:00-17:54Z was an info-level entry "order confirmation email sent to \"reed@example.com\"" at 16:23:06Z, i.e. a false positive on the digits 500 inside its microsecond timestamp, not an error.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config injects the fault flags for this demo: paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%") and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable") are each state "ENABLED" with defaultVariant "off"; every other listed flag (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) is also defaultVariant "off".

Cluster-wide the only deployments are kube-system (coredns, metrics-server), local-path-storage (local-path-provisioner) and 21 otel-demo demo workloads; there is no deployment named checkout-service or payment-service, and the checkout/payment deployment env carries PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 and only demo settings (no adyen or external provider endpoint).

The POST /api/checkout 500s are a consequence of payment-service's outbound calls to the external payment provider adyen-eu timing out at 30s, after which checkout-service tripped its circuit breaker for payment-service at a 36% failure rate; the deepest cause the evidence supports is adyen-eu being slow/degraded (its own status page acknowledged degraded mode with a 620-deep retry queue). Not confirmed by metrics or traces, and the moment the degradation began is not observed.

A payment-service retry queue at depth 620 may be prolonging the timeouts and holding checkout requests past its own 30s provider timeout, thereby sustaining the 500s; the queue's effect on request latency is not measured in any available evidence.

A flagd fault-injection flag on the payment path caused the checkout 500s: rejected, because paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable are both defaultVariant "off" in otel-demo/flagd-config, and no flag referencing checkout or payment is switched on.

A local pod fault (crash, OOM, restart, or an unavailable payment endpoint) in the readable cluster caused the checkout 500s: rejected, because both pods are Running and ready with 0 restarts and no previous container instance, the payment containers keep logging successful "Transaction complete." charges, Service payment resolves to 10.96.207.54:8080 and checkout to 10.96.172.147:8080, and no NetworkPolicy exists in otel-demo.

The workloads visible in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1 do not show the failure the log index describes: checkout and payment pods are ready with 0 restarts, payment logs only successful charges, and no object in the cluster references adyen or services named checkout-service/payment-service, so the emitting workloads could not be tied to the inspected objects.

Confirm the impact and its start with the payment service's own signals once Prometheus is reachable: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} by status_code, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{rpc_service=~".*adyen.*"} for the 30s client latency, and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count for checkout's /api/checkout 5xx ratio, comparing a pre-incident baseline before asserting any latency trend.

Treat the provider as the failing dependency: verify adyen-eu status, review payment-service's 30s provider timeout/retry-queue backlog (depth 620) and checkout's circuit-breaker thresholds, and consider decoupling checkout from the provider timeout so POST /api/checkout fails fast instead of surfacing 500 after 30s.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the whole run (get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no error-rate, request-count or latency series for checkout/payment or the adyen client calls were checked; there is no baseline against which to call anything a trend.

Jaeger was unreachable for the whole run (traces_list_services, traces_search, traces_search_by_tags all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level parent-child edge from checkout to payment to adyen-eu could be established; the checkout->payment->adyen chain rests on the log message text alone.

The index holds only 4 documents across the entire authorized window, so the first occurrence of the provider timeout, the volume of failed POST /api/checkout requests, and any subsequent recovery inside 2026-11-23T16:54:17Z-17:54:25Z are unknown; ERROR series that are absent are unknown, not zero.

The emitting services in the logs (checkout-service, payment-service) and the provider adyen-eu do not correspond to any object in cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1 (the only deployments are otel-demo demo workloads); a cluster-wide ConfigMap search for adyen/checkout-service/payment-service matched nothing, so those workloads' status and logs could not be read.

No Kubernetes events were returned for the authorized window (events query status no_data), so rollout, eviction or probe evidence is unavailable; a pod-level filter on the checkout pod for error/warn/circuit text also returned no_data and cannot be used to conclude absence.
The exact time the adyen-eu degraded-mode setting/policy changed and the declared fault itself were not observed; only payment-service's 17:24:17Z acknowledgement of degraded mode is visible.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change can be correlated with the incident.
Secrets and any provider credentials/endpoints of the real payment-service stack are not readable here, so the actual adyen integration configuration could not be verified.
next_steps: Verify adyen-eu provider status and incident timeline for 2026-11-23 15:00-18:00Z against the retry-queue depth reported by payment-service.
When Prometheus is reachable, chart traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} status_code breakdown and the adyen rpc_client_duration series for 15:00-18:00Z with a preceding baseline.

Identify the real owner of the checkout-service/payment-service workloads that emit into app-267-prod-logs (cluster id/namespace labels in that logging pipeline) so their pods, events and logs can be inspected.

adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620

view.cannot_prove: A document that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only size documents are shown, and retention, ingest delay and the index pattern can leave gaps. The time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily when the event happened. total and aggregations cover only the matched indices inside the query window.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
